title: Christian Warrior Women: A Guide to Taking Back Your Faith, Family & Future
author: Lisa Hawkins
target_audience: Women interested in reclaiming their faith and spiritual authority
Readers navigating personal, family, or faith-based challenges
Small groups, Bible study participants, and ministry leaders
core_themes: Spiritual warfare and victory through faith
Empowerment of women in Christian contexts
Rediscovering and strengthening personal identity in Christ
Overcoming obstacles and reclaiming one’s future
primary_purpose: To equip Christian women with spiritual tools and biblical insights for overcoming personal, familial, and faith-based challenges, guiding them to reclaim authority over their lives and futures through practical application of faith principles.

structure_format.organization: Organized into thematic chapters with Scripture references, personal stories, reflective questions, and action steps

key_concepts_lessons: Faith is an active, not passive, force in combating life’s struggles.
Women have spiritual authority and a vital role in family and faith communities.
Healing and restoration are possible through trust in God and biblical truth.
Recognizing and taking action against spiritual complacency.
Practical steps (prayer, Scripture, community) to reclaim one’s life.
notable_features: Emphasis on women’s stories and testimony-based teaching
Focus on modern applications of biblical spiritual warfare
Designed for personal study or group discussion
cultural_historical_context: Released amid a broader movement of Christian women’s empowerment in the late 2010s, the book addresses contemporary struggles faced by women in faith, family, and society, responding to renewed interest in spiritual intentionality and overcoming generational challenges.
reception_impact: Appreciated by Christian women's ministries and small groups for practical, relatable guidance
Lauded for authenticity and actionable faith-building exercises
Contributed to ongoing dialogues regarding women's roles and spiritual authority in Christian circles
Some feedback notes the book’s direct, faith-specific perspective may be less relevant for those outside evangelical or charismatic traditions
